title: Private migration snapshot orchestrator and rollback policy
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Private (VPC / on-prem) customers sometimes require complex, multi-step migrations (schema changes, agent binaries, config rearrangements) that must complete with zero or controlled downtime. Current tooling supports scripted migrations but lacks a first-class coordinator that can take crash-consistent snapshots, coordinate staged rollouts, surface progress telemetry, and perform safe automated rollback when health gates fail.

Goal: Implement a Migration Snapshot Orchestrator (MSO) for Redwood Private that: 1) captures crash-consistent snapshots (metadata + state checksums) before any disruptive step; 2) coordinates staged execution with canary groups and rollout gates; 3) exposes progress and health signals to Console / runbooks; 4) supports deterministic rollback policies (reverse steps or restore snapshots) with clear operator controls and safety timeouts.

Design notes / approach: MSO is implemented as an operator-style controller inside the customer’s control plane (or the private agent fleet). Key behaviors: snapshot capture (agent-local checkpoints + central manifest stored in customer-controlled object store or etcd), preflight checks (capacity, disk, feature compatibility), staged rollout groups (canary → progressive), gate evaluation (health probes, SLO windows, manual approval hooks), rollback triggers (failed probe, degraded latency, explicit abort), and post-migration verification (consistency checks, sampling of model outputs). The operator will emit structured events and telemetry to the Console integration and write an audit trail to the upgrade manifest.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Push vs pull coordination: push simplifies sequencing but requires operator connectivity; chosen hybrid model where MSO writes manifest and agents pull tasks so operator outages are less catastrophic. 2) Snapshot storage: prefer customer-managed object store for data locality and compliance; provide an encrypted fallback inside private control plane if not available. 3) Rollback mechanism: full reverse migration for non-destructive ops, snapshot restore for destructive schema changes. Reverse migrations are safer when available but may not exist for every change.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- MSO can create and validate a snapshot manifest for a small test cluster (3 nodes) and store it in the configured object store.
- A staged canary rollout completes successfully with gate checks passing and progress appearing in Console.
- When a simulated health gate fails, MSO triggers an automated rollback according to the configured policy and records the action in the audit trail.
- Operators can manually pause/resume and force-rollback from Console + CLI.
- E2E test run against an on-prem cluster is reproducible and documented in the runbook.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped initial MSO MVP to snapshot + canary + rollback-by-restore. Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya (SRE), Anil (Security). Action: Diego to prototype manifest format and agent pull API.

2026-02-20 - Prototype update: agent pull API sketch available in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-mso/pull/12. Early feedback: need idempotency token per task; Priya requested explicit circuit breaker for disk-pressure conditions.

2026-02-28 - Design review: Confluence spec posted https://confluence.redwood.local/display/ENG/MSO-spec. Decision: use customer object store by default; add encrypted fallback. Security requested threat model for stored snapshots (in flight + at rest).
2026-03-01 - SRE note: added health probes (control-plane latency, inference error-rate, KV cache hit-rate) as rollout gate candidates. We agreed a 5-minute SLO window for canaries in MVP.

2026-03-03 - Implementation: initial operator code merged to feature branch. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-mso/pull/34 (operator scaffolding), https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/78 (agent task runner). Diego: instrumentation wired to v0 telemetry endpoint; needs Console-side wiring.

2026-03-04 - PM feedback (Priya Brooks): add explicit user-visible rollback reasons and link to runbook steps in UI. Also requested short-circuit to snapshot-restore if reverse-migration script is missing.

2026-03-05 - Risks and next steps: need integration test for snapshot integrity under partial network partition (test infra ticket created). Plan to run a full canary on staging private cluster next week. Diego to follow up on RBAC scopes for operator service account.
